title: Three Sessions of Mind-Recollection by Master Zhongfeng, Annotated
author: Annotated by Zhanran
excerpt: Note: The heading of each discourse has been added for convenient reading; it is not part of the original text.

inline.s: Preface
Main Text
Note: The heading of each discourse has been added for convenient reading; it is not part of the original text.

Mind-Recollection at Three Sessions” is one of the Buddha-recitation methods of the Pure Land school. It was advocated by National Master Zhongfeng of the Yuan dynasty, and its main purpose is to be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and to depart forever from the boundless sea of karma. National Master Zhongfeng wrote two works concerning the Three Sessions of Mind-Recollection: one is the “Manual of the Rites of the Three Sessions of Mind-Recollection,” used for gathering together in self-cultivation; the other is the “Liturgy of the Three Sessions of Mind-Recollection,” used for performing rites to liberate the dead, guiding departed spirits to rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Both are composed of seven parts — chanting the sutras, Buddha-recitation, discourses, practice of the Way, repentance, making vows, and hymns of praise — and each session includes these seven items. This essay is an annotation of the
Liturgy of the Three Sessions of Mind-Recollection
discourse section.
[The three sessions] The times of morning, noon, and sunset. [Mind-recollection] A single mind fixed upon Amitabha Buddha, without a single straying thought.

First session rite: The discourse instructs the practitioner (including both the living and the dead) that in the Land of Ultimate Bliss there is none of the host of sufferings, and that a person of the Way who would seek the road home has only to settle his own mind amid the dusts and so extinguish the deluded mind. Living beings suffer without end because of greed and desire, and greed arises from forgetting one’s own nature and letting stray thoughts run wild. To leave suffering and gain bliss and be reborn in the Pure Land, faith, vows, and practice must all be complete. Therefore the practitioner should hold deep faith and make earnest vows, and uphold the Name of Amitabha Buddha with a single mind unconfused; at the end of life he shall be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitabha Buddha.

Second session rite: The discourse instructs the practitioner (including both the living and the dead) that mind, Buddha, and living beings are not three and not different, and reveals the mind-only Pure Land and the self-nature Amitabha Buddha. Although the Dharma-nature is thus bright and still, yet non-arising gives rise to arising, and the fruits of karma are manifestly present. Thus living beings transmigrate through the six realms and revolve through the four modes of birth. The practitioner should therefore reveal and repent, washing away the stains of karma, increasing his roots of good, and, letting go of this retributive destiny, be reborn in the Pure Land.

[The four modes of birth] Womb-born, egg-born, moisture-born, and transformation-born. Womb-born beings take form within the mother’s womb and are then born, such as humans; egg-born beings take form within an eggshell and are then born, such as birds; moisture-born beings rely on dampness to receive their form, such as insects; transformation-born beings rely on nothing but karmic power and appear suddenly, such as the devas, the hell-dwellers, and humans of the beginning of the aeon. [Retributive destiny] The karmic cause of retribution, that is, the lifespan of a single lifetime.
Third session rite: The discourse instructs the practitioner (including both the living and the dead) on the vast merit of the six-syllable sacred name “Namo Amitabha Buddha”:
A single utterance

of the name of Amitabha Buddha can sit across and sever the six sense-roots, wiping away the heavy offenses of birth and death of eight hundred thousand myriads of kotis of aeons. It is like a clear jewel cast into muddy water; the muddy water cannot but become clear. Therefore the practitioner needs only to lift up the Buddha-name, and straightway there is no other thought. Like the great blade of Tai-e, it severs afflictions; like a great wheel of flame, it burns away ignorance. Until the mind reaches single-mindedness and the two — subject and object — are both forgotten. Thus recollecting the all-virtuous great name of Amitabha Buddha, with vow and practice both deep, the merit is never wasted; one is certain to be conceived in the lotus womb, to depart forever from the sea of karma, and to realize directly avivartika (the stage of non-retrogression), perfectly attaining the supreme bodhi (becoming a Buddha).

blocks.text: Hymn of Praise on the True Incense of Precepts and Samadhi

inline.s: The true incense of precepts and samadhi, when burned, rises straight to heaven.
This disciple, in earnest devotion, burns it in the golden censer.
In an instant the fragrant haze pervades the ten directions.
In former days Yasodhara escaped calamity and dissolved the hindrances of misfortune.
Namo to the Bodhisattva-Mahasattva of the fragrant cloud canopy
(recited three times)
[True incense of precepts and samadhi] Burning incense purifies the air, whereas the true incense of precepts and samadhi purifies the body (conduct), the mind, and the social environment. [Ruo (
ruò
)] to burn. [Yin-yun (
yīn yūn

)] to pervade. [In former days Yasodhara escaped calamity and dissolved the hindrances of misfortune] In former days Yasodhara observed the precepts and samadhi with utmost strictness. Bathed in the true incense of precepts and samadhi — like one perfumed by incense whose body bears the fragrance — under the protection of the majestic light of fragrance she escaped calamity and dissolved the hindrances of misfortune. This is a shining example for later learners, and so it is specially cited in the hymn.

The story of Yasodhara: Before Shakyamuni Buddha left home he was Prince Siddhartha, and Yasodhara was his wife. Six years after the prince left home, Yasodhara gave birth to a son, Rahula. Everyone said, “How can this be? The prince has been away from home for six years, and yet Yasodhara has given birth to a child! Surely she has not kept to her virtue!” At that time the customs of India were extremely harsh; a woman had to be chaste, and if she were not, she would be burned alive. So they dug a pit, set the wood within it alight, and were about to burn Yasodhara and Rahula alive. Then Yasodhara said, “If I am chaste, then neither I nor my child will be burned, and a lotus flower will spring forth to protect us.” Having spoken, she gathered her mind in one place and leapt in. In truth a lotus flower appeared from the fire, catching and holding up the mother and child. Thus Yasodhara, because she strictly held the precepts and samadhi, “escaped calamity and dissolved the hindrances of misfortune.” Why could Yasodhara escape the calamity by saying she would? Because in both her past lives and this life she held the precepts and samadhi with utmost strictness.

blocks.text: The Sea of Awakening Arose From the Void

inline.s: The sea of awakening arose from the void; the waves of karma in the Saha world flow on;
If a person would reach the other shore, the Land of Bliss holds the boat of return.

The sea of awakening arises depending on the void, while in the Saha world (this shore) the waves of karma flow every which way; for you to ascend to the other shore of nirvana, the Land of Ultimate Bliss holds the boat for returning home (becoming a Buddha).

This verse is the guiding principle of the whole piece: for the beings of the unseen (the dead) and the seen (the living) in the Saha world, to escape transmigration and realize the fruit of Buddhahood, the most excellent path is to recite the Buddha’s name and be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
“The sea of awakening arose from the void:”
The sea of awakening arises depending on the void,
and the myriad things are suddenly manifest,

and only then do the two shores (this shore of birth and death and the other shore of nirvana) begin to be divided. Between the shore of birth and death and the other shore of nirvana the sea of awakening lies across. The “sea of awakening” is a metaphor: the journey of awakening is like crossing a great sea — perilous and long. The ancients said:
“Borrow a raft in the deluded ford; cast a boat in the sea of awakening.”
[The sea of awakening arises depending on the void] This is the first deluded stirring of a single thought, whereby one enters the dream of ignorance (see further the
Dream of Ignorance
essay
), and falsely manifests objects. The Surangama Sutra says:
“In delusion there is empty space; depending on space the worlds are established; when thought settles it becomes lands; consciousness is the living beings.”
“The waves of karma in the Saha world flow on:”
This Saha world in which we dwell (this shore of birth and death),
the karma created by living beings rolls like a surging torrent, fierce and overwhelming, overflowing into calamity.
“If a person would reach the other shore:”
You should ascend to the other shore of nirvana (become a Buddha).
[Ruo ren (if a person)] You, you all; the meaning is the same as “ruo bei.” Here “ruo” means you, you all.
“The Land of Bliss holds the boat of return:”

The Land of Ultimate Bliss holds a jeweled boat that goes straight to the other shore of nirvana. Living beings reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss attain the stage of non-retrogression (avivartika) and realize Buddhahood in a single lifetime. Hence it is said, “The Land of Bliss holds the boat of return.” This is a metaphor: once one reaches the Land of Ultimate Bliss, there is a jeweled boat that, riding the wind and cleaving the waves, crosses the sea of awakening and goes straight to the other shore of nirvana, without needing to swim across alone (swimming alone across the sea is a metaphor for the common path relying wholly on one’s own power to remove afflictions and sever ignorance — a course of incomparable peril and difficulty). Hence Universal Worthy’s Ten Great Vows lead back to the Land of Bliss.

[The boat of return] The boat for returning home. Living beings are originally Buddha; now, dwelling deludedly in the Saha world, they are wandering in a foreign land, and ascending to the other shore of nirvana (becoming a Buddha) is returning home. [Living beings are originally Buddha] The Perfect Awakening Sutra says:
“Then you know that living beings are originally Buddha; birth, death, and nirvana are like a dream of last night.”

[Birth, death, and nirvana like a dream of last night] Birth, death, and nirvana are all matters in the dream of ignorance. Now that the dream of ignorance has ended, looking back at past affairs is like the dream of last night. (See further the
Detailed Explanation of the Perfect Awakening Sutra

[Universal Worthy’s Ten Great Vows lead back to the Land of Bliss] Universal Worthy Bodhisattva, by means of the Ten Great Vows, leads back to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, encouraging Sudhana the youth and the forty-one stages of Dharma-body great beings of the Hua-yang sea-host to direct their merit toward rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, in order to perfect the fruit of Buddhahood. On this, Master Yinguang gave this instruction:

“In the Hua-yang sea there are limitless Pure Lands, yet one must direct one’s merit toward rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. From this it may be known that rebirth in the Land of Bliss is the mysterious gate of leaving suffering
(an extremely wondrous method)
, and the shortcut to Buddhahood.”

(From “Resolving Doubts on the Pure Land”) [The Hua-yang sea] Hua-yang is an abbreviation for the lotus-store world, the land of Vairocana Buddha, the true body of Shakyamuni Tathagata. Because within the lotus are concealed worlds as numerous as dust-motes, it is called the Hua-yang sea. [An extremely wondrous method] The wonder and subtlety of the Buddha-recitation method can be known only by Buddha and Buddhas.

blocks.text: Discourse One: Reverently Hearing the Wondrous Dharma

inline.s: The King of Dharma benefits beings, with compassion and wisdom vast and deep,
Pervading the ten directions, among the unseen and the seen there is no separation.

Amitabha Buddha saves living beings; his compassionate mind and wondrous wisdom are deep, vast, and endless, reaching to the ten directions; in the unseen world and the seen world there is no obstruction.

[The King of Dharma] The Buddha, sovereign and free over the Dharma, is called the King of Dharma. Here it refers to Amitabha Buddha. [Wu (the beings)] The multitude of beings; for example, “the expectations of the multitude.” Here “wu” means all living beings. [Mi (
mǐ
)] without, none.
Now, receiving the patron
so-and-so
, reverently on behalf of
so-and-so
, at the occasion of
so-and-so

, I specially invite this mountain monk to ascend the seat, and in reliance upon the teaching of the Buddha to perform the Three Sessions of Mind-Recollection rite. This departed spirit, meeting such a splendid karmic occasion, should of himself be solemn in bearing and demeanor, and come before the seat, reverently hearkening to the wondrous Dharma, with single mind accepting the deliverance.
Today, receiving the kindness of the patron
so-and-so
, reverently on behalf of
so-and-so
, at the very occasion of
so-and-so

, I specially invite this mountain monk (a humble term) to ascend the Dharma seat and, according to the Buddha’s teachings, to perform the Three Sessions of Mind-Recollection rite. You departed spirits, encountering such an excellent karmic occasion, should be solemn in dress and bearing, come beneath the seat, reverently listen to the wondrous Dharma, and with single mind and utmost sincerity accept the deliverance.
[The patron] The donor who gives vegetarian food offerings. [The mountain monk] A monk of the wild mountains (a humble self-reference).

blocks.text: Discourse Two: Burning Incense as Offering

inline.s: This single petal of incense: its root coils beyond the aeon, its branches spread through the world of dust; it was not brought forth by heaven and earth — how could it belong to the creative work of yin and yang?

This single petal of incense (the true incense): its root coils back to before the beginningless aeon, its branches and leaves spread and flourish in the human world; it was not brought forth by heaven and earth, nor created and evolved by yin and yang.

[Incense] Here incense signifies the true incense of precepts and samadhi, following the above “Hymn of Praise on the True Incense of Precepts and Samadhi.” [A petal of incense] Because the form of incense resembles a melon petal, it is called a petal of incense. The Grove of Matters in Patriarchal Halls says:
“Venerable masters of ancient and modern times, when holding up incense, mostly say ‘a petal.’”
[World of dust] The human world.

Burned in the censer, it is offered with single-minded devotion. To the ever-abiding Three Jewels, to the myriad spirits of the sea of lands, to the guide of the Land of Bliss Amitabha Buddha, to Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta, to the pure sea-host — all rely upon this true incense, and to all alike we make offering.

The incense (true incense) burns in the censer of the mind, offered sincerely with single devotion. The ever-abiding (the monastery), the Three Jewels (the Buddha-jewel, the Dharma-jewel, the Sangha-jewel), all living beings of the ten directions, the guide of the Land of Bliss Amitabha Buddha, Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta, and the pure sea-host of bodhisattvas — all rely upon this true incense, and to all alike we make offering.
sea of lands
The full term is “the great sea of lands,” referring to the worlds of the ten directions.
[The myriad spirits] All sentient living beings.

blocks.text: Discourse One: Merely Settling One’s Own Mind

inline.s: Why is the world called Ultimate Bliss? Because none of the host of sufferings can invade it;
If the person of the Way would seek the road home, he has but to settle his own mind amid the dusts.

Why is the world called Ultimate Bliss? Because none of the host of sufferings can invade it; if the practitioner would seek the road home, this road is: but to settle his own mind amid the six dusts (extinguish the deluded mind).
[Why is the world called Ultimate Bliss? Because none of the host of sufferings can invade it] In the Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra, the Buddha says:
“Why is that land called Ultimate Bliss? Because the beings of that land have none of the host of sufferings but receive only manifold bliss; therefore it is called Ultimate Bliss.”

[The six dusts] Form-dust, sound-dust, fragrance-dust, taste-dust, touch-dust, and dharma-dust. “Dust” has the sense of defilement, meaning it can defile the pure minds of people so that the true nature cannot be manifested. They are also called the six objects, that is, the objects upon which the six sense-roots (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind) rely.
This verse is the prelude; the discourse that follows explains how to settle one’s own mind.
Mind after mind is Buddha; the ti-wei and su-lao all arise from milk; Buddha after Buddha is only mind; hairpins, bracelets, vases, and plates all come from gold.
“Mind after mind is Buddha; the ti-wei and su-lao all arise from milk:”
To transform the deluded mind into the true mind is to be Buddha. Know that the bodhisattvas of the various stages, and even the Buddhas, all come from ordinary people!
[Mind after mind is Buddha] To transform the deluded
mind
(the first word “mind”) into the true
mind

(the second word “mind”) is to be Buddha. [The ti-wei and su-lao all arise from milk] This is a metaphor: the Buddha and living beings are different states of the self-nature. The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch says:
“When the self-nature is deluded, that is a living being; when the self-nature is awakened, that is a Buddha.”

[The ti-wei and su-lao all arise from milk] When milk is refined one obtains butter (lao); when butter is refined one obtains su; and when su is refined one obtains ti-wei. The Indians not only regard ti-wei as “the first supreme flavor in the world,” but also hold it to have extremely high medicinal value. Here milk, butter, su, and ti-wei are used to metaphorically express the different stages of practice: milk represents ordinary people, butter and su represent the bodhisattvas of the various stages, and ti-wei represents the Buddha.
“Buddha after Buddha is only mind; hairpins, bracelets, vases, and plates all come from gold:”

For living beings to become Buddha, they too have only to transform the deluded mind into the true mind, because ordinary people, the bodhisattvas of the various stages, and even the Buddhas are identical in nature, differing only through the delusion or awakening of the self-nature.
[Buddha after Buddha is only mind] The principle-identity
Buddha
(the first word “Buddha,” which is a living being), to become the ultimate-identity
Buddha

(the second word “Buddha,” the Buddha of fully perfected fruit), likewise has only to transform the deluded mind into the true mind. [Hairpins, bracelets, vases, and plates all come from gold] The gold vessels — hairpins, bracelets (chuan, bangles), vases, and plates — are all likewise made of gold; their nature is the same, only their forms differ. A metaphor: living beings and the Buddha are identical in nature; the former is deluded, the latter awakened. [The principle-identity Buddha and the ultimate-identity Buddha] The first and the last of the two stages among the six identities of Buddha.
[The six identities of Buddha] Established by Great Master Zhizhe of the Tiantai school, to show the stages by which an ordinary person cultivates and realizes the fruit of Buddhahood:

First, the principle-identity Buddha. All living beings, though they transmigrate through the six realms and dwell daily amid the dust-and-toil of afflictions, turning their backs upon the awakened substance, nevertheless fully possess the merit of Buddha-nature; hence they are called “the principle-identity Buddha.”
The Buddha Speaks the Maha Parinirvana Sutra says:
“Know that liberation is itself the Tathagata. That which is the Tathagata is the Tathagata-nature, which is present within the bodies of all living beings.”

Second, the name-identity Buddha. Whether from a good teacher or from the scriptures, having heard of the inherent, unborn, and undying Buddha-nature, and through the name having comprehended and understood that all dharmas are Buddha-dharmas and that all living beings can become Buddhas — nodding in assent, with a sudden opening of understanding — one is called “the name-identity Buddha.”

Third, the contemplation-practice identity Buddha. This is the position of the five grades, the outer-ordinary stage of the Perfect teaching. Not only comprehending the name, but further, in accordance with the teaching, cultivating contemplation, knowing that all dharmas are the Buddha-dharma; the contemplation of the mind is clear, the wisdom of principle responds; hence one is called “the contemplation-practice identity Buddha.”

Fourth, the semblance-identity Buddha. This is the stage of the ten faiths, the inner-ordinary position of the Perfect teaching: the first faith severs the delusion of views, the seventh faith severs the delusion of thought, and the eighth, ninth, and tenth faiths sever the delusion of dust-and-sand. The practitioner at this stage, in contemplation and practice, the more he contemplates the clearer, the more he stills the more serene; though he has not truly awakened or truly realized, yet in the principle he resembles it, as if truly realized; hence he is called “the semblance-identity Buddha.”

Fifth, the partial-realization identity Buddha. This is at the last thought of the ten faiths: breaking one portion of ignorance and realizing one portion of the three virtues, one enters the first dwelling and realizes the Dharma body; from then on one becomes a Dharma-body great being. From the first dwelling onward, each stage breaks one portion of ignorance and realizes one portion of the three virtues, up to the stage of equal enlightenment, passing through forty-one stages altogether and breaking forty-one portions; hence one is called “the partial-realization identity Buddha.”

Sixth, the ultimate-identity Buddha. This is when, from equal enlightenment, one breaks the final portion of ignorance; then delusion is exhausted and truth is pure, and one thoroughly realizes the inherent thusness Buddha-nature of one’s own body, entering the stage of wondrous enlightenment and becoming a Buddha; hence one is called “the ultimate-identity Buddha.”
A journey of a hundred thousand kotis, yet east and west are not separated; within the twelve hours, the ordinary and the holy share the same road.

Although the Saha world and the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss are separated by a hundred thousand kotis of Buddha-lands, in fact they are not divided; throughout the twenty-four hours, Amitabha Buddha is with me.
This means: once awakened, the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is right before one’s eyes, and Amitabha Buddha is with me day and night.
[East and west]
The Saha world (east) and the Land of Ultimate Bliss (west).
[The twelve hours]
The twelve double-hours. In antiquity a full day and night was divided into twelve double-hours. Here “twelve hours” means the whole day and night.
[The ordinary and the holy]“
The ordinary” refers to the living beings of the Saha world; “the holy” refers to Amitabha Buddha.

Bowing the head, palms joined, before the white-jade hair, bright as stars and radiant as the sun; singing hymns of praise to the purple-golden countenance, like a peal of thunder and a crash of lightning.

Bowing the head and joining palms in worship of Amitabha Buddha, one’s own mind is clear and bright, like the brilliance of stars, the splendor of the sun; singing hymns in praise of Amitabha Buddha, the sound is like a peal of thunder, a crash of lightning, echoing through the universe.
[The white-jade hair, the purple-golden countenance]
Amitabha Buddha has a purple-golden body, with a white-jade hair between the brows; therefore this represents Amitabha Buddha.
[Ting] A thunderbolt.
The cool moon! It is contained in all waters; the cloud of merit! There is no mountain it does not crown.

[The cool moon, contained in all waters] The bright moon hangs in the sky, its reflection appearing in a thousand rivers and ten thousand waters. A metaphor for Amitabha Buddha dwelling in the heart of every living being: if one single-mindedly recites the Buddha’s name, there is a meeting of mind and the Way. [The cloud of merit, no mountain it does not crown] A metaphor for Amitabha’s merit being present everywhere, benefiting every living being.

The fragrant elephant fords the river; with one raising of the great name one transcends the two deaths; the Kalavinka emerges from its shell; a thousand utterances of the lovely name surpass all other sounds.

[The fragrant elephant fords the river] A fragrant elephant (a great elephant) fording a river cuts its flow and reaches the bottom. A metaphor: Buddha-recitation severs birth and death. [With one raising of the great name one transcends the two deaths] Chanting Amitabha’s name severs the two deaths (the death of delimited life and the birth-and-death of transformation). [The death of delimited life] Living beings in the three realms and six paths, because their life spans and bodies are delimited by their good and evil karma, have a birth-and-death called “the death of delimited life.” One who has ended the death of delimited life escapes transmigration and leaves the three realms. [The birth-and-death of transformation] The sages of the three vehicles, having severed the delusions of views and thought and ended the death of delimited life, in the course of practice gradually dissolve delusions and increase realization; this shifting from delusion to awakening differs in each stage, and the transition from one stage to the next is like a passage through death; hence it is called “the birth-and-death of transformation.” One who has ended the birth-and-death of transformation perfectly realizes the fruit of Buddhahood. [Kalavinka] An abbreviation of the Kalavinka bird, whose song is supremely beautiful. The Surangama Sutra says:
“The immortal song of the Kalavinka pervades the worlds of the ten directions.”

[The Kalavinka emerges from its shell] A metaphor: a living being becoming a Buddha-recitater is like the Kalavinka emerging from its shell. [A thousand utterances of the lovely name surpass all other sounds] The sound of Buddha-recitation surpasses all other sounds, meaning the Buddha-recitation method is more excellent than all other methods.
The lowly feelings can only suppose
cǔn
, to infer)
what is hard to conceive, yet with a single thought turning back the light it is easy to go. In the ultimate sense it is not outside the mind; it is clearly right before the eyes.

Ordinary people are utterly unable to fathom the wonder and subtlety of the Pure Land method with their emotive consciousness; but if they but turn their thought back to the sacred name of Amitabha Buddha, they will very easily be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. For in the ultimate sense the Land of Ultimate Bliss is not outside the mind; it is clearly right before one’s eyes.
If this is truly so, then this present assembly, recollecting Amitabha in the three sessions of Buddhist rite, no longer needs to be concerned with realization and practice.

If they can indeed hear the above discourse, and in a single thought turn back the light and settle their own minds (extinguish the deluded mind), then today’s three sessions of Mind-Recollection rite no longer need to concern themselves with how to cultivate and how to realize.

[If this is truly so] Truly so. [Not concerned with realization and practice] If the departed spirit truly, in a single thought, turns back the light and settles its own mind, it is at once delivered and no longer needs cultivation and realization. Hence the following passage — “As for the phase ‘personally receiving the prediction,’ how is it proclaimed? The wind sings in the trees a thousand kinds of music,
the fragrance steeps each pool with four-colored lotus” — is the presiding master bestowing the prediction that the delivered departed spirit will be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[The wind sings in the trees a thousand kinds of music, the fragrance steeps each pool with four-colored lotus]
This depicts the scenery of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[The four-colored lotus] The Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra says:

“In the ponds the lotus flowers are as large as cartwheels; blue light for the blue, yellow light for the yellow, red light for the red, white light for the white, subtly wondrous, fragrant, and pure.”
As for the phrase “personally receiving the prediction” — how is it proclaimed?
The wind sings in the trees a thousand kinds of music; the fragrance steeps each pool with four-colored lotus.

[As for the phrase “personally receiving the prediction” — how is it proclaimed?] How is the phrase “personally receiving the prediction” proclaimed? [Prediction] The sense of recording a name: the Buddha, for a living being who has aroused the great mind, records in advance his name — after so many aeons, in such a place and such a land, becoming such a Buddha. Here the prediction is rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. [Personally receiving the prediction] The Bodhisattva Jueming Miaoxing, in his Certain Guidelines on the West, gave this instruction concerning his own past “personally receiving the prediction”:
“Long ago, in the time of Emperor Ming of the Jin, I received the body of a poor boy. Because of poverty I made the great vow, saying: ‘Because I
(owing to)
past karma
(the karmic offenses of former lives)

, I receive this bitter retribution. If today I do not see Amitabha Buddha and am not born in the Land of Bliss, and do not perfect all merit, then even if I lose my life I shall never retreat or rest.’ Having made this vow, for seven days and seven nights I single-mindedly and earnestly recollected, and at once my mind opened and I saw Amitabha Buddha’s excellent marks and radiant light pervading the worlds of the ten directions. Before the Buddha I personally received the prediction, and afterward at age seventy-five I sat upright and passed away, and was in fact born in the Land of Bliss.

You should be single-minded in this method, firmly cultivating it; you will certainly not be mistaken. If your resolve is firm, you need not wait for the next life to be born; even in the present you shall see the Buddha, just as I did in former years.”
(See further the
Certain Guidelines on the West (Annotated)

) [The wind sings in the trees a thousand kinds of music; the fragrance steeps each pool with four-colored lotus] These two lines depict the scenery of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss: the wind blows the rows of trees and produces every kind of wondrous sound, and the four-colored (blue, yellow, red, white) lotus flowers perfume the seven-jeweled ponds everywhere. This is the prediction: one is certain to be born in the Land of Bliss.

blocks.text: Discourse Two: Realizing the Non-arising Dharma

inline.s: All the various sufferings arise entirely from greed and desire; do you not know from what greed and desire arise?
Because one forgets the self-nature Amitabha Buddha; stray thoughts running every which way are forever the devil.
All

the various sufferings arise entirely from greed and desire; and from what then do greed and desire arise? The answer lies in the next two lines: “Because one forgets the self-nature Amitabha Buddha; stray thoughts running every which way are forever the devil.”

[The self-nature Amitabha Buddha] The self-nature of living beings inherently possesses the Tathagata’s wisdom, virtue, and power, not two, not different from Amitabha Buddha; hence it is called the self-nature Amitabha Buddha. It is only that living beings are deluded and cannot realize it.
The Diamond Sutra says:
“If you see that all forms are non-forms, then you see the Tathagata.”
(See further the
Detailed Explanation of the Diamond Sutra
) The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch says:
“Know your own mind; see your own nature.”
These are the essential methods for not forgetting the self-nature Amitabha Buddha. (See further the
Detailed Explanation of the Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch
Because one forgets the self-nature Amitabha Buddha; stray thoughts running every which way are forever the devil

Because one forgets that the self-nature is the true self, and takes this body and mind as “I” (entering the dream of transmigration), one gives rise to feelings of love and aversion, and deluded thoughts (stray thoughts) run wild. Thus greed and desire arise along with feelings and thoughts (one is possessed by the devil), and driven by greed one creates every kind of karma; through karma one receives retribution, drawing upon oneself all the various sufferings, and birth and death transmigrate without end.
The Perfect Awakening Sutra says:
“All living beings, from the beginningless past, are all manner of inversion, like a lost man who mistakes all four directions
(just as a lost traveler confuses east, south, west, and north)
, falsely taking the four elements as the form of self and the shadows of the six dusts as the marks of the mind. ... Because of this false existence they revolve in birth and death.”
(See further the
Detailed Explanation of the Perfect Awakening Sutra
[Stray thoughts] Thoughts that are not right thought.

[The four elements] All material things in the world are composed of the four elements — earth, water, fire, and wind — hence the term “great”: the great earth, great water, great fire, great wind. Earth has hardness as its nature, water wetness, fire warmth, wind motion. Here the four elements refer to the human body.

[The shadows of the six dusts] The many thoughts produced when the six sense-roots meet the six dusts; and because these thoughts are all false and unreal, they are called “the shadows of the six dusts” — the phantom reflections of meeting the six dusts.
The core of this chapter is the realization of the non-arising Dharma.
[Realizing the non-arising Dharma] Realizing the non-arising Dharma (the real marks of all dharmas). On the real marks of all dharmas, see further the
Real Marks of All Dharmas
essay. [The non-arising Dharma] All dharmas are phantoms; originally they never arose, hence they never cease. The Diamond Sutra says:
“All forms are false and delusive.”
The Vimalakirti Sutra,
Chapter Nine on Entering the Non-dual Dharma-gate, says:
“Dharmas originally are unborn; now they are also unceasing.”
The teaching says: non-arising yet arising, and the Dharma-nature is bright and still; arising yet non-arising, and the fruits of karma are manifestly present.
